thread:
ops-bot: ALERT — spike in 5xx rate from ap-south-1 gateway cluster. automatic paging triggered. (metric: gateway_5xx_rate > 4% for 3m)
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-AP-SOUTH-5XX — paging on-call. page routed to infra-oncall.
infra-oncall: I'm on it. grabbing initial metrics. can someone confirm customer-facing impact? @support? :eyes:
support: Seeing increased error reports from a handful of customers — FinanceProd and MobileAuth show ~15–25% 502s in the last 5m. CS is triaging.
sanjay: oncall here — joining. outline: collect traffic, check connpool, NAT, and gateway backend health.
ida: quick health snapshot: ap-south-1 EDGE-GW cluster shows 3 pods with high accept queues, TCP retransmits up, backend qps unchanged. redis caches look fine.
maria: logs show a surge of long-lived upstream connections to our ml-worker fleet (seq length > avg). suspect KV cache TTL storm from a batch job in region.
kevin: can we get the gateway logs (tail) for the last 2 minutes? I'll grep for 502/504 patterns.
sanjay: grabbing logs now — running: ```kubectl logs -n edge gw-ap-south-1 --since=2m | egrep "HTTP/1.1 \"5..|timeout|connreset"```
kevin: results: many upstream timeouts to ml-worker: `dial tcp x.x.x.x:443: i/o timeout` and 502 response bodies referencing `upstream read timed out`.
ida: network telemetry shows a NAT gateway (ap-south-nat-1) CPU spike -> conntrack exhaustion warnings. conntrack counts near max.
infra-oncall: ok priority mitigation: start draining traffic from ap-south-1 edge pool and steer to ap-southeast-1 + us-east-1. can ops run the drain and steer?
sanjay: initiating gradual drain: ```/scripts/edge-drain --region ap-south-1 --grace 30s --target-regions ap-southeast-1,us-east-1```
ops-bot: DEPLOY-BOT: traffic steering policy update applied (policy id p-9831). rolling change over 1m.
maria: while drain proceeds, can we increase conntrack table size on NAT? ops: name the nodes.
kevin: raising conntrack temporarily on the NATs: ```for i in nat-1 nat-2; do ssh $i sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144; done```
ida: conntrack bump applied on two NATs, counts falling, but still high. we should also scale up the gateway pool to absorb remaining.
infra-oncall: scaling gateway replicas by +2 in ap-south-1 to reduce accept queue. ```kubectl scale deployment/gw-ap-south-1 --replicas=6 -n edge```
sanjay: note: autoscaling for ml-workers in ap-south is throttled due to quota bump delays. for faster relief, we're enabling fallback routing at the API proxy (route to model-variant cpu-optimized) for non-low-latency customers.
maria: toggling fallback flag for model routing: ```PATCH /v1/routes/fallback?region=ap-south-1 {"enabled":true, "target":"model-small-cpu"}```
support: Communicated to affected customers: interim message sent — "We are investigating increased error rates in ap-south-1; some requests may be slower or return 5xx. We're routing traffic to alternative regions and expect improvement in ~10–15 minutes." :phone:
kevin: post-drain metrics: 5xx rate dropped from 6.3% -> 2.1% in 3m after steering started. p50/p95 latencies stable in fallback regions.
ida: but some persistent 502s remain for customers pinned to ap-south-1 dedicated pools (reserved capacity). need a manual migration for those customers.
infra-oncall: reaching out to account teams for manual migration. @maria, can you prepare a migration snapshot for FinanceProd?
maria: preparing snapshot, will coordinate with sales/CS. estimate 20–30m for full migration to ap-southeast-1.
sanjay: opened a follow-up runbook item: check for long-lived upstream connections from batch jobs (possible TTL misconfig causing cache misses). stopping a suspicious batch job now.
ops-bot: JOB-BOT: batch-job analytics-job-42 terminated by ops for debugging.
kevin: after killing the job, KV cache miss rate decreased and ml-worker request tails went down. 5xx rate now 0.9% region-wide.
ida: confirming NAT CPU normalized and conntrack usage back to safe thresholds.
infra-oncall: summary so far: cause: localized conntrack exhaustion + long-lived upstream connections driven by a batch job -> NAT overload -> upstream timeouts -> gateway 5xx. mitigations: drained/steered traffic, bumped conntrack, scaled gateway, killed offending job, enabled model fallback.
sanjay: customer impact: intermittent 5xx for some dedicated customers and ~15–25% 502s for a few tenants during spike window. overall error budget exceeded on ap-south-1 for 12m.
maria: recommended next steps: postmortem, migrate dedicated tenants, add automated conntrack bump/remediate preemption, and add a circuit-breaker on gateway upstreams based on conntrack metrics.
infra-oncall: immediate action items assigned: [sanjay] verify migration tickets; [maria] finish snapshots and CS handover; [kevin] instrument better upstream timeout seals; [ida] write quick runbook appendix for NAT conntrack.
sanjay: handing over to on-call evening shift. i'm signing out in 5. @infra-oncall take it from here. :wave:
infra-oncall: taking over. will monitor for 30m then move to monitoring mode if stable. prepping incident timeline for postmortem.
support: closing customer loop: will update customers in 30m or earlier if fully recovered.
ops-bot: Incident status changed -> mitigated. INC-2026-AP-SOUTH-5XX moved to monitoring.
kevin: logs/metrics snapshot stored: s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2026-AP-SOUTH-5XX/snapshots/6854321123.tar.gz
ida: leaving a short note: possible long-term fixes: increase NAT pool redundancy, enable conntrack autoscale alerts (threshold 70%), and a faster off-ramp for dedicated tenant migration.
maria: adding to backlog: implement upstream circuit-breaker that reduces new upstream dial attempts when conntrack > 75% and fallback to alternate region.
infra-oncall: thanks all. creating postmortem stub and linking to timeline, will tag owners. good catch catching the batch job. :thumbsup:
support: Incident thread will be linked in the customer incident page and CS comms. closing the Slack thread after final customer update.
ops-bot: NOTE: pager duty records updated. escalation channel closed.
infra-oncall: final status: mitigated, monitoring, action items filed. will follow up with a formal postmortem doc in #postmortems within 48h.
notes: Contains root message + all replies in chronological order. Includes bot messages, on-call handoff, mitigation steps, commands, and customer comms.
